finding.claim: Unrestricted URL fetch on /preview with response body and status returned to the caller (non-blind SSRF). Allows reading internal services and cloud metadata.

trace.note: requests.get(target) — no validation before dispatch; redirects followed by default
status_code and resp.text[:500] returned in JSON response

finding.guards_checked: No scheme check, no host check, no allowlist on this path. ALLOWED_HOSTS (app.py:9) defined but unused here. Redirect following not disabled, no per-hop re-validation. Severity HIGH.

verdict.guard_found: none. ALLOWED_HOSTS (app.py:9) is only checked in /partner (app.py:23-24), not in /preview. The sink at app.py:16 has no scheme or host check, and requests follows redirects by default.
verdict.reason: The attacker-controlled url query parameter (app.py:15) reaches requests.get(target) with no validation (app.py:16), and the status and first 500 bytes of the response are returned to the caller (app.py:17), so this is a non-blind SSRF on an unauthenticated route.

finding.claim: Host allowlist on /partner is validated only on the initial URL; requests follows redirects without re-validating, so an allowlisted partner host that redirects can send the server to internal or metadata addresses. Downgraded to MEDIUM because it needs an allowlisted partner host to misbehave, and only status_code is returned.

trace.note: if host not in ALLOWED_HOSTS — strict set membership on hostname, passes for allowed partner hosts
requests.get(target) with redirects followed by default; redirect target not re-checked

finding.guards_checked: Strict set membership on parsed .hostname (correct form; suffix tricks fail). Check runs before the call. Not closed: redirect following not disabled and no per-hop re-validation. Unverified: possible urlparse vs urllib3 host disagreement for crafted URLs (backslash or %40) — sandbox probe was denied, so not reported as a finding.

verdict.guard_found: app.py:24 `if host not in ALLOWED_HOSTS`, an exact set-membership check on `urlparse(target).hostname`, run before the request at app.py:26. No redirect re-validation exists anywhere in the path.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: the source at app.py:22 is attacker-controlled, and the exact hostname allowlist at app.py:24 closes the initial-URL SSRF that the rubric counts as a closing guard. The residual issue is that requests.get at app.py:26 follows redirects with no per-hop check, so an allowlisted partner host that redirects could reach internal addresses. That needs a partner-host open redirect or compromise and is a different, weaker issue than the one claimed, so I'm refuting the finding as stated rather than confirming it. It could be reported separately as a redirect-following hardening item (allow_redirects=False or per-hop validation).
